extracted.intended_audience: UPSC / civil services aspirants and students studying Indian institutions
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic/UPSC-prep overview of the Press Council of India covering its history, mission, composition, functions, powers, limitations, funding, and complaint procedure relevant for exam preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission of the Press Council of India
rubrics_metrics.description: The Press Council of India's mission is to safeguard the independence of newspapers and news agencies, establish a code of conduct for these entities and journalists, and promote elevated professional standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to ensure newspapers, news agencies, and journalists uphold high standards of public taste while balancing rights and responsibilities; monitors developments that could impede supply/dissemination of news of public interest; addresses concentration of ownership and other factors impacting independence; promotes harmonious relationships among those involved in newspaper or news agency production and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Press Council of India
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI is led by a chairman (by convention a retired judge of the Supreme Court) and consists of 28 members, of whom 20 represent the press (represented by press agencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member breakdown given: Two Members of the Rajya Sabha; Three members of the Lok Sabha; 7 Working Journalists (other than newspaper editors); 6 Newspaper Editors; 3 Persons having extensive knowledge of Public Affairs; 1 Person in charge of the News Organization; 6 Persons engaged in the business of managing newspapers. Members serve for a term of three years. A retiring member is eligible for renomination for not more than one term (max 2 consecutive years) — (verbatim wording from page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of PCI Chairman
rubrics_metrics.description: The chairman of the Press Council of India is selected by the Speaker of Lok Sabha, the Chairman of Rajya Sabha and one member of the PCI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By convention the chairman has been a retired judge of the Supreme Court of India (page notes this convention separately under composition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding of the Press Council of India
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI is funded by revenue collected as a fee levied on registered newspapers on the basis of their circulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It does not levy a fee on newspapers which have a circulation of less than 5,000 copies (verbatim).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of the Press Council of India
rubrics_metrics.description: The functions include monitoring anything that can restrict free flow of information, creating codes of conduct for journalists and news agencies, providing training, encouraging news-related research, ensuring newspapers operate independently, and ensuring good news quality for the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists functions explicitly: Keep an eye on anything that can restrict the free flow of information or news; Create a code of conduct for Journalists; Create a code of conduct for news agencies; Providing training to new journalists; Encourage technical and other news-related research; Make sure that newspapers continue to operate independently; Ensure good news quality for the general public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of the Press Council of India
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI can enquire into complaints it receives, summon witnesses, demand copies of public records, issue warnings, criticize (admonish) the guilty (journalist, newspaper, agency, or editor), and censure; decisions taken are final and cannot be appealed before a court of law (per page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page emphasizes its powers to issue warnings, admonishments, and censures; it can summon witnesses and demand public records; any editor or journalist can complain to PCI about professional misconduct or violation of journalistic ethics by another editor or journalist. Note also elsewhere the page describes the PCI as 'predominantly advisory' with limited authority to enforce compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of PCI's authority and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI has limited powers to enforce its guidelines: it cannot penalize anyone for violation of guidelines and its enforcement powers are largely confined to the print media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: it only has powers to enforce standards on the print media; powers are restricted with respect to electronic media like radio, television and the Internet; restricted to journals, magazines and newspapers. The article also notes PCI often struggles with backlog and delays and 'lacks punitive power to ensure compliance with its directions' (Ajay Goswami v. Union of India reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint procedure — initial step and who can complain
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Section 14 of the Press Council Act, 1978, anyone can file a complaint with the Press Council against a newspaper, editor, or journalist for breach of recognized ethical standards in publication or non-publication of news, articles, cartoons, or advertisements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complaint process requires that the complainant must first write to the editor, highlighting the objectionable content and giving them a chance to address and rectify the matter; if dissatisfied, the complainant can escalate to the Press Council. This initial-editor step may conclude the complaint if the editor responds satisfactorily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint content and supporting materials required
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint submitted to the Press Council must include identifying details and evidence: name and address of the editor, journalist, or newspaper involved, specification of how the content is objectionable under the Press Council Act, 1978, and other particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainant should include copies of correspondence with the editor and a declaration that no legal proceedings are pending. The page states these particulars are required for a complaint to be processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing complaints (limitation periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per the Press Council (Procedure for Inquiry) Regulations, 1979, complaints against dailies, news agencies, and weeklies must be filed within two months, while in all other cases complaints must be filed within four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing requirement is presented as a strict filing window under the cited regulations; complainants should note the differing deadlines by category of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-judicial/adjudicatory role and remit
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI is a quasi-judicial body and acts as a watchdog for the press: it adjudicates accusations of ethics violations and press freedom violations brought against and by the press, and is entrusted with ensuring Freedom of Expression under the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While described as quasi-judicial and a regulator that defines and disseminates professional standards, the page also stresses that PCI predominantly serves in an advisory capacity and that implementation depends on involved parties complying with its recommendations.
